query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Aluminum pack cementation can improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr by forming a protective alumina scale.
generation.conditions: Temperature: 800-1000 °C, Atmosphere: air, Exposure time: 5-100 hours, Loading: tensile stress up to 500 MPa
generation.mechanism: Formation of a protective alumina scale that prevents oxygen diffusion into the alloy
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxygen resistance, reduced oxidation rate, and preservation of mechanical properties
generation.boundary: Temperature: 800-1000 °C, Atmosphere: air, Exposure time: 5-100 hours, Loading: tensile stress up to 500 MPa
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of aluminum pack cementation in improving oxygen resistance may depend on the specific processing conditions and the resulting microstructure of the alumina scale

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled exposure of aluminum pack cementation-treated and untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr to air at 800 °C for 100 hours, followed by tensile testing at room temperature and 1000 °C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated material exhibits no significant improvement in oxygen resistance or mechanical properties compared to the untreated material, the hypothesis is falsified
